name: Guideline Forest (Guideline Forest: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Branching Experience-Induced Guidelines)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2506.07820 [cs.AI]). Submitted 9 Jun 2025 (v1), v2 10 Jun 2025, v3 last revised 7 Feb 2026. No peer-reviewed venue identified as of this survey; appears to be a preprint only. [uncertain on any accepted conference/journal venue]
authors_affiliation: Jiaxiang Chen (Fudan University; equal contribution), Zhuo Wang (Fudan University & SII; equal contribution), Mingxi Zou (Fudan University), Qifan Wang (Meta), Zenglin Xu (Fudan University & SAIS; corresponding/senior author). Primary affiliation: Fudan University.
paper_url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07820 (PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.07820 ; HTML v3: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07820v3 ; DOI: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2506.07820)
code_url: N/A - no official code repository is linked in the paper (arXiv 'Links to Code' / CatalyzeX entry not populated; no GitHub URL stated in the text). [uncertain]
task_domain: Multi-step LLM reasoning: mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH-500) and code generation (MBPP, HumanEval). Framed as improving reasoning quality (not knowledge-grounding QA, not embodied/web agents). Tasks are reasoning/code-generation with verifiable final answers.
problem_setting: Offline-to-online, single-model (with an optional multi-model collaboration extension) supervised setting. A training phase uses labeled (question, answer) pairs to build a memory of verified gold reasoning trajectories; an inference phase retrieves from this frozen memory and reasons over a new problem. Supervision is available (ground-truth labels used both to verify/regenerate training trajectories and to filter what gets stored). Two LLMs are used in the pipeline: GPT-4o-mini for reasoning generation and GPT-4o for verification. The default deployment is single-agent step-wise branch reasoning over one model; an optional Multi-Inference Collaboration extension assigns different guideline branches to different LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) and aggregates their step-level candidates by weighted voting. The memory grows during training in a closed loop but is frozen for the reported test-time evaluation.
what_is_retrieved: experiences / trajectories: verified, label-consistent 'gold reasoning' trajectories (problem + step-wise solution + embeddings) of past solved training problems. These retrieved trajectories are then abstracted into structured 'guidelines' (reusable, high-level step-wise reasoning plans) that steer the new reasoning. So the retrieved unit is a past reasoning trajectory; the USED unit is a distilled guideline induced from it.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic experience memory the system itself writes (a repository M_mem of verified gold reasoning trajectories built during a training/collection phase via a closed-loop self-improving process). Explicitly contrasted with conventional RAG that retrieves a static external knowledge corpus: here retrieval targets accumulated REASONING EXPERIENCE, not docs/KB. Construction is offline-induced during training then frozen at test time; growth happens within the training loop, so grounding is a self-built growing memory (dominantly experience-grounded, not a static external corpus).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval objective: for each test problem the system retrieves the top-k (default k=3) most semantically similar verified positive samples by cosine similarity, then aggregates their solution steps into a guideline. The ablation (Fig.4a / retrieval-scale study) frames k as a precision/quality trade-off (too few -> overly specific/misaligned paths, too many -> generalization noise), with k=3 best, but the mechanism is still a fixed-size top-k, not a completeness-driven minimal-set or variable-size recommendation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: yes, Retain: yes]. Retrieve: top-k cosine retrieval of verified gold trajectories. Reuse: trajectories are abstracted into guidelines and reused to steer step-wise reasoning (not verbatim ICL; an induced/adapted reuse). Revise: a stepwise self-refinement mechanism revises intermediate outputs, and label-guided regeneration revises incorrect training trajectories. Retain: verified trajectories are appended to memory (closed-loop growth). All four canonical CBR phases are effectively realized, though under non-CBR terminology.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the paper does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed via retrieval-augmented generation/reasoning, exploratory reasoning (CoT/ToT/FoT), ensemble/collaborative inference, and a latent-trajectory marginalization formulation. It nonetheless realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain CBR mechanisms (storing past solved cases, retrieving similar ones, abstracting/adapting, retaining new solutions) under another name.
retrieval_unit: Full reasoning trajectory / case (problem + step-wise solution): the retrieved unit is a verified gold reasoning trajectory z=(z_1,...,z_T) paired with its problem x. From the top-k retrieved trajectories the system induces guideline(s) g=(g_1,...,g_T), an abstract step-wise reasoning plan. So retrieval granularity = full trajectory (problem-solution episode); the derived/used granularity = guideline-rule (per-step reasoning plan).
index_source: Growing, offline-induced memory repository M_mem built during a training/collection phase from labeled training data (GSM8K 500, MATH-500 ~700 across categories, MBPP 100, HumanEval 30 training instances). Construction is a closed self-improving loop (CoT -> label-guided regeneration -> optional ToT exploration -> optional memory-guided refinement; only correct trajectories retained). The store grows during training and is then frozen for test-time inference. Not a static external corpus; not built at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index over trajectory/problem embeddings (text-embedding-3-small embeddings; stored as problem, steps, embeddings; cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor retrieval). No graph, hierarchy, or cluster topology described. (The 'forest' in the name refers to the branching reasoning structure at inference, not to the index topology.)
retriever_type: Dense retriever using off-the-shelf OpenAI text-embedding-3-small embeddings with cosine similarity for top-k nearest-neighbor search over the gold-reasoning memory. Not BM25, not learned/RL-trained, not generative.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the retriever itself (off-the-shelf frozen text-embedding-3-small embeddings; fixed cosine top-k; no contrastive training, no LM-feedback, no RL). The supervision/quality signal is applied to WHAT populates the index (only label-consistent, verified-correct gold trajectories are retained via label-guided generation and GPT-4o verification), not to the retriever's ranking function.
query_construction: Raw problem statement is used as the query/key. At inference the new input problem x is embedded with text-embedding-3-small and matched against stored problem/trajectory embeddings by cosine similarity. No query decomposition, expansion, intent extraction, or thought-conditioning of the retrieval query (retrieval is a single one-shot lookup per problem; the per-step branching/aggregation that follows does not re-query the memory).
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is performed per test problem using the whole problem as the query to fetch the top-k gold trajectories, from which guidelines are induced. The subsequent multi-branch step-wise reasoning does NOT issue fresh per-step retrievals against the memory; branching/aggregation operate on the already-induced guidelines.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval from the gold-reasoning memory happens once per problem at the start of inference (to induce the guidelines). It is not iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or router-gated. (Within the training loop, a memory lookup is also used to help refine hard training cases, but that is part of memory construction, not test-time retrieval.)
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / unconditional: one retrieval is triggered at the beginning of solving each new problem (to build its guideline set). No token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated request triggers retrieval. (During training, retrieval from M_mem is triggered when verified trajectories are insufficient / for harder instances, a construction-time heuristic.)
reranking: None - no explicit reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker). The top-k positive samples are taken directly by cosine similarity. (A separate step-level aggregation selects among candidate reasoning branches, but that is candidate-step selection during generation, not retrieval reranking.)
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose / distillation into guidelines: the retrieved trajectories are not injected verbatim but are abstracted via a Guideline Generation Prompt into a concise core-problem + step-wise reasoning plan, then expanded via a Guideline Rewriting Prompt into 3 diverse branch variants. This is a distill-then-diversify refinement of retrieved content (not simple rerank/compression, and no explicit distractor filtering at retrieval time).
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tools/skills or tool descriptions are indexed or retrieved. Retrieval items are natural-language reasoning trajectories embedded with text-embedding-3-small.
index_content_separation: Partial / induced-abstraction rather than progressive disclosure: stored entries hold problem + steps + embeddings; what is injected at inference is the INDUCED guideline (a distilled abstraction), not the raw heavy trajectory. There is no explicit lightweight-index-then-load-heavy-content (SOP-index-then-content) mechanism; the abstraction is generated on the fly via prompting rather than stored as a separable index layer.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - not a tool-retrieval system; no live tool index or RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling protocol. The memory is an internally managed dense vector store that grows during the training loop only.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no tools retrieved, so no inter-tool dependency modeling.
how_retrieved_used: Case adaptation + prompt augmentation (guideline-steered generation): retrieved gold trajectories are abstracted into structured guidelines (high-level step-wise plans), rewritten into M (~3) diverse branch variants, and each guideline step is injected into the LLM prompt (Guideline Execution Prompt) to steer the corresponding reasoning step. Thus retrieval is used as an instructional scaffold that guides step-wise generation, not as verbatim few-shot exemplars and not as a training signal (no weight updates at inference).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan-then-branch: a single retrieval induces a guideline set, which is the high-level plan; reasoning then proceeds per-step in a multi-branch manner where each guideline branch independently proposes a candidate step z_t^(m), each candidate is optionally self-refined, and the M candidates are aggregated into a single unified step z_hat_t that becomes shared context for the next step. This is a step-wise interleaved branch-and-aggregate procedure (forest-of-paths) rather than MCTS/tree search; complexity O(MT) for M branches over T steps.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step: branching, self-refinement, and aggregation are interleaved at each reasoning step (each guideline branch proposes a candidate step; candidates are refined and aggregated per step). Retrieval from memory, however, is per-problem (once), so retrieval-vs-reasoning interleaving is coarse (one retrieval) while the branch/aggregate search is fine-grained per step.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted abstraction + diversification + execution-feedback-style self-correction: the retrieved case is (1) abstracted into a guideline via an LLM prompt (not verbatim ICL), (2) rewritten into multiple perspective variants, (3) executed step-by-step with a lightweight self-correction/refinement at each step and aggregation-based selection among branches. No RL reuse-finetuning; adaptation is prompt-driven (induce -> rewrite -> execute -> refine -> aggregate).
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy / guideline (free-text structured step-wise plan): what is injected is an induced guideline with a 'Core Problem' and numbered reasoning steps (e.g., <step 1>, <step 2>, ...), rewritten into 3 diverse variants. Not raw trajectory text, not an executable program/skill object, not latent/soft tokens. (For code tasks the guideline is still a natural-language reasoning plan; the final answer is code.)
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled reusable reasoning workflow / guideline: the paper explicitly distinguishes concrete instance-specific trajectories (what is stored/retrieved) from abstract reusable guidelines (what steers reasoning). The operative abstraction level is a distilled strategy/reusable step-wise plan (mid-high abstraction), deliberately capturing general reasoning structure rather than exact solutions.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Several: (1) memory contains only verified, label-consistent gold trajectories (incorrect trajectories discarded; GPT-4o verification) so the retrieval source is clean; (2) retrieval-scale ablation tunes k=3 to balance specificity vs generalization noise; (3) guideline abstraction strips instance-specific details, reducing overfitting to a single retrieved case; (4) multi-branch diversity + step-wise aggregation (confidence-based scoring/voting) provides ensemble-like robustness against individual-path errors; (5) step-wise self-refinement corrects intermediate errors before they accumulate. No retriever-side relevance evaluator or distractor-aware SFT at retrieval time.
memory_type: Episodic experience memory of verified gold reasoning trajectories (a 'reasoning experience repository' M_mem). Stored as concrete episodic trajectories (problem + steps + embeddings); guidelines are derived from it at inference rather than stored as a separate skill-library/workflow/graph/latent memory.
write_back: True - all verified (label-consistent, correct) reasoning trajectories are appended to the memory repository: M_mem <- M_mem U {(x^(i), z^(i)*)} (Eq.2), forming a self-improving loop where accumulated experience continuously expands the reasoning repository. Write-back happens during the training/collection phase.
online_growth: Partial - the store GROWS during the training/collection (closed-loop self-improving) phase as more verified trajectories are added, but it is FROZEN for the reported test-time inference (guidelines extracted from training samples guide test inference; no evidence the memory is written during test-time deployment). So growth is offline/training-time, not test-time-online.
write_back_trigger: On-success only (label-verified): a trajectory is written to memory iff it produces the correct ground-truth answer (verified, with GPT-4o verification). Incorrect initial trajectories are first regenerated via label-guided generation (best-of-n, up to three rounds) and ToT exploration for harder instances; only the resulting correct trajectories are retained, and failed cases are discarded. No per-step or unconditional write-back; no storing of failures.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only. Failed/incorrect trajectories are explicitly discarded and never stored or retrieved. There is no failure/negative-experience memory and no success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval. Errors are handled transiently via label-guided regeneration during construction and step-wise self-refinement at inference, but failures are not retained as corrective cases.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only growth: verified trajectories are appended to M_mem (Eq.2). No described dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forget-prune of existing stored entries; the repository monotonically accumulates. (Individual stored trajectories are not mutated in place after writing.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No - retrieval/case-selection is a fixed off-the-shelf cosine-similarity top-k (text-embedding-3-small), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or trained selector). Selection signals (label-consistency for retention, k tuning, branch aggregation) are heuristic/supervision-based, not a trained retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Optional cross-model sharing via the same induced guidelines: the Multi-Inference Collaboration extension assigns the (shared) guideline branches to different LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B), each of which generates step-level candidates following its assigned guideline; these are aggregated by weighted voting (Eq.4, uniform weights w=1), reaching e.g. 90.32% on number-theory tasks. This is sharing of reusable guidelines/experience across heterogeneous models (model-agnostic, transferable priors), though the memory itself is a single shared repository, not per-agent private memories.
benchmarks: GSM8K (grade-school math word problems; 500 train / 1,319 test), MATH-500 (competition math across 7 categories: algebra, precalculus, prealgebra, counting & probability, geometry, intermediate algebra, number theory; ~100 train sampled per category, full benchmark for test), MBPP (Python program synthesis; 100 train / 341 test, following AFlow), HumanEval (Python code generation; 30 train / 130 test, following AFlow).
benchmark_family: QA/math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH-500) + code generation (MBPP, HumanEval). Spans the math-reasoning and code families (SWE-bench-style repo tasks are NOT used; MBPP/HumanEval are function-level code-gen). No web/embodied/tool/memory-RL benchmarks.
baselines: Direct: IO (input-output prompting). Exploratory reasoning: CoT (Wei et al. 2022), CoT-SC / Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2022), ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b), ToT (Yao et al. 2023a), FoT / Forest-of-Thought (Bi et al. 2024). Search-based: AFlow (Zhang et al. 2024, MCTS-based agentic workflow generation). Also compared across backbones (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct) and against guideline-enhanced versions of CoT/ReAct/ToT.
key_metrics: Solve Rate (%) for math (GSM8K, MATH-500) = fraction of problems with correct final answer; pass@1 for code (MBPP, HumanEval) = fraction passing all test cases on a single generated solution. Plus tokens-per-problem and an accuracy-cost utility 'Acc-1kTok' = Acc - Tokens/1000 for the efficiency analysis.
headline_result: With GPT-4o-mini, Guideline Forest reaches GSM8K 93.5%, MATH-500 69.2%, MBPP 81.6%, HumanEval 95.4% (avg 84.9%), outperforming all baselines on average (best baseline AFlow 84.1 avg) and achieving the best single results on GSM8K, MATH-500, and HumanEval (on MBPP 81.6% is slightly below AFlow's 83.4%). Most-cited single figure: MATH-500 69.2% vs ToT 65.2 / FoT 65.8 / AFlow 65.6 with GPT-4o-mini.
ablations: (1) Mechanism ablation on MATH-500 subdomains (Table 4): Full 69.20 vs w/o multi-guideline 61.39, w/o aggregation 62.19, w/o refinement 64.63 - all three components contribute (e.g., Geometry 41.66 -> 53.66 with multi-path; Prealgebra 76.83 -> 80.20 with refinement). (2) Retrieval scale (Fig.4a): k=3 positive samples is optimal (too few -> overly specific, too many -> generalization noise). (3) Path diversity (Fig.4b): multi-path > single-path. (4) Stepwise refinement (Fig.4c): ~+4% avg. (5) Aggregation strategy (Fig.4d): stepwise aggregation > final-step-only, ~+7% absolute. (6) Backbone scaling (Table 2): improves with GPT-4o > GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-32B. (7) Guideline-enhanced baselines (Table 5): CoT 57.8->59.8, ReAct 58.0->66.0, ToT 65.2->66.0; Ours 69.8. (8) Multi-model collaboration (Fig.5): cooperation best, 90.32% on number theory. (9) Cost ablation (Table 3, Num.Th.): GF 12.6k tokens / 85.48% / Acc-1kTok 72.88, best utility.
evaluation_decoupling: No - only end-to-end task metrics (Solve Rate / pass@1) plus token-cost are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval completeness) are reported separately; the retrieval-scale ablation (k) is measured by downstream solve rate, not by retrieval quality.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-focused (final Solve Rate / pass@1). Some process-adjacent analyses: training-accuracy-vs-iteration curve (Fig.3) showing improvement from CoT -> label guidance -> ToT stages; step-wise aggregation/refinement ablations probing intermediate-step quality; and qualitative case studies (Fig.6, Appendix) illustrating step-level reasoning and refinement. No formal step-wise retrieval-accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Explicit accuracy-cost analysis (Table 3, Num.Th. of MATH-500): Guideline Forest uses 12.6k tokens/problem (vs ReAct 5.4k, ToT 7.2k, FoT 21.8k) at 85.48% accuracy (vs ReAct 67.74, ToT 75.81, FoT 83.87), giving the best Acc-1kTok utility 72.88 (vs ReAct 62.34, ToT 68.61, FoT 62.07). About 40% fewer tokens than FoT while outperforming it. Inference cost scales linearly O(MT) with M~3 branches and T reasoning steps (vs FoT's O(KMT)). No wall-clock/latency or dollar figures reported. [uncertain on exact latency/API-dollar numbers]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: top-k=3 positive samples retrieved per problem (k=3 optimal per ablation); guideline rewritten into M~3 diverse branches executed per step. Maximum input lengths capped at 400 tokens for MATH-500/GSM8K and 600 tokens for MBPP/HumanEval. Selection is fixed-k by cosine similarity (not adaptive/precision-driven, not reranked-then-truncated).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - uses existing benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP, HumanEval), not a benchmark-construction paper. Train/test splits used: GSM8K 500/1319, MATH-500 ~100-per-category train / full test, MBPP 100/341, HumanEval 30/130.
builds_on: RAG (Edge et al. 2024 GraphRAG; Guo et al. 2024 LightRAG; SlimRAG 2025) reframed from knowledge to reasoning retrieval; CoT (Wei et al. 2022) and CoT-SC/Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2022); ToT (Yao et al. 2023a) used both as a baseline and as a structured-exploration component during training; FoT/Forest-of-Thought (Bi et al. 2024) for branching reasoning; ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b); AFlow (Zhang et al. 2024) for workflow/data-split protocol; ensemble learning (bagging/boosting/random forests/mixture-of-experts) as the conceptual basis for branch aggregation; BoostStep (Zhang et al. 2025a, step-level case-library retrieval) and AdaS (Hu et al. 2024) as related step-retrieval/adaptive-compute work.
contrasts_with: Exploration-based reasoning (CoT, ToT, FoT) that builds trajectories from scratch per instance with unguided test-time search and no experience reuse; workflow/search-based methods (AFlow, HaIR-ICL via MCTS, WorkflowLLM) that learn fixed/heuristic workflows with high search cost and limited transfer; conventional RAG that retrieves external knowledge documents (vs retrieving reasoning experience); pure test-time sampling ensembles (Self-Consistency, multi-LLM Avengers/SMACS) that lack experience-grounded structured branching. Guideline Forest instead retrieves verified reasoning trajectories, distills reusable guidelines, and aggregates step-wise at O(MT) cost.
lineage: Group B (RAG for reasoning / task-solving) intersecting experiential/episodic-memory reasoning. Lineage: RAG (knowledge retrieval) -> reasoning retrieval / experience reuse; CoT -> ToT/FoT branching -> Guideline Forest, which adds a verified-gold-reasoning memory plus guideline induction and step-wise branch-and-aggregate. Positioned as 'reasoning-experience retrieval': retrieving and reusing verified gold trajectories abstracted into structured branching guidelines that drive reasoning, bridging RAG, exploratory reasoning, and ensemble/collaborative inference.
